title: ABC Batteries
prompt: Our client ABC Batteries is an Indian battery manufacturer whose profits have been declining for the past 6 months. Identify the core issue and suggest recommendations.

facts.reveal: Two kinds: AA/AAA for remotes and electronic appliances, and D-cell for torches.
D-cell battery sales have been declining.
ABC manufactures. Its sales executives reach regional distributors and wholesalers, who supply the retailers: local electrical shops.
India only. If the candidate infers that D-cell buyers are mainly in Tier-II cities and rural areas, confirm it.

facts.asks: Industry-wide or just us; the competitive landscape
facts.reveal: Just ABC. Two major players in D-cells: ABC has 30% share, XYZ has 50%, and the rest is fragmented. XYZ's profits have risen over the same period.
The decline is across India; some geographies are more affected than others.
Costs are constant; D-cell revenue has declined.
The number of units sold has decreased.

facts.asks: Our product and price compared with XYZ
facts.reveal: Comparable product specifications and post-purchase benefits. ABC sells at a 5% lower retail price, and always has.

facts.asks: Where to focus, once the candidate has laid out the customer's purchase journey
facts.reveal: Focus mainly on awareness of the product.

facts.asks: Awareness, the point of sale, retailers or the sales team
facts.reveal: In one of the major markets ABC's sales executives left the company. The new ones lack the retailers' trust, so retailers push XYZ to customers who do not ask for a brand.
facts.condition: Only once the candidate looks at awareness or the point of sale

facts.asks: What XYZ has done differently, or why buyers keep choosing XYZ
facts.reveal: In the past year XYZ launched torches pan-India, sold bundled with its D-cell batteries. Customers repurchase the same brand of cells when they run out.
facts.condition: Only once the candidate looks at awareness or the point of sale

outOfScope: Any rupee figure: sales, profit, or the size of the decline

crux.statement: The switch happens at the shop counter, not in the product. Two causes: lost retailer push after sales-team churn, and XYZ's torch bundle locking in repeat purchases.
crux.clue: XYZ grows while ABC falls, though ABC's product is comparable and cheaper. So the gap is in how the battery reaches the buyer.
crux.test: Remove "XYZ's profits rose" and the candidate can blame a shrinking market. Remove "comparable and 5% cheaper" and they chase price or quality. Both facts are load-bearing.

paths: Profit → revenue → volume → demand → customer journey (need, awareness, purchase) → awareness of a low-involvement buyer
Down the distribution chain: sales executive → distributor → retailer

wrongTurns.text: Product quality or leakage (no data, and flat costs argue against it)
Electrification killing torch demand (that would hit XYZ too)

answerKey: Answer the torch bundle: launch a torch line if feasible, or partner with torch brands; advertise the D-cell as price-competitive and compatible with every torch
Rebuild retailer trust: experienced local sales hires, key opinion leaders, cash or trade discount schemes, trust-building workshops

close.condition: The candidate names both causes, or finds the second after one nudge.
close.prompt: Now suggest some recommendations on how to resolve this.

anchors.s5: Stays on product or generic marketing. The interviewer has to reveal both causes.
anchors.s7: Uses the competitor comparison to reach the retailer. Finds one cause; recommendations are generic.
anchors.s9: Goes to the point of sale unprompted, finds both causes, and ties a fix to each. Checks whether a torch launch is feasible before recommending it.

verifierFlags.decision: Keep it qualitative. Nothing is added.
